q: How do I turn a refrigerant top-up invoice (R-32, R-410A, R-134a) into CO2e?
title: Refrigerant top-up invoice to CO2e
short: Multiply the kilograms of gas charged into the equipment by that gas's 100-year global warming potential (GWP). For a blend such as R-410A, first work out its GWP from the component shares. The result is Scope 1 CO2e. State whether you used IPCC AR5 or AR6 values.
audience: Facility and EHS managers at Indian factories and cold stores

p: A sealed AC or chiller only needs gas when some has escaped. When a technician recharges it to its rated charge, the kilograms added are a fair measure of what leaked since the last service. This is the simplified mass balance the GHG Protocol's HFC guidance uses for equipment you operate. HFCs are Kyoto gases, so the result goes in your Scope 1 total.

sections.h: What to take from the invoice
ul: The gas name or R-number, for example R-32, R-410A or R-134a.
Net kilograms charged into the equipment. If the invoice shows cylinders, use the net gas weight, not the gross cylinder weight.
The equipment and site serviced, so you can place it in the right facility and year.
Leave out gas for a new installation's first charge, gas bought and kept in stock, and gas recovered and sent back. None of these is leakage.

p: Use one basis for the whole inventory. Many programmes now ask for AR6; some buyer templates still use AR5. Write the basis next to the figure.

If you control the equipment, the leak is your Scope 1, even when an outside AMC contractor does the service and bills you. If the landlord runs a central chiller for the building and you only pay a share, it is usually the landlord's Scope 1, and your share can sit in Scope 3. R-22 and other HCFCs follow a different rule; they are reported outside the Scope 1 total.

example.title: Worked example: one year of service invoices at a cold store
lines: Top-ups: R-410A 12 kg (split ACs), R-134a 5 kg (chiller), R-32 3 kg (office ACs)
Same gas, same kilograms: the AR6 figure is about 17% higher, so the basis must be stated
example.note: For comparison, 31.6 t CO2e is roughly what 44,500 kWh of grid electricity emits at 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25. Small refrigerant top-ups can matter.

senseible: Senseible reads service and purchase invoices and keeps them as evidence. It calculates refrigerant emissions only when you supply the measured data, such as the gas and kilograms charged, and does not treat a gas purchase alone as leakage.
